commit.message:
v1.91.350.0 feat(review): GSTA-167 variant G reviewer stack: blocking floor in both voices, one batched specialist, data-file classifier (#3660)

* feat(review): variant G part 4: data files no code names are docs in classifyDiff, untested state-matrix cells map below the floor per cell (GSTA-167 PR-a)

Part 4a: lib/review-depth.ts owns DATA_PATH (JSON, JSONL, NDJSON, CSV, TSV, raster
images; YAML, TOML and SVG stay code) and applies the data rule only in classifyDiff,
to candidates lib/review-collect.ts finds no non-docs consumer for (git grep of
basenames at head, merge base and, live, the working tree; data-to-data chains four
deep; over 2,000 candidates keeps all code; a grep failure fails closed). classifyPath
and every path-only caller are unchanged; the receipt gate scan decides through
gateScanNeeded (path-only), so it cannot be skipped. gstack-ship-preflight computes
RUNTIME_LINES with classifyDiff over gstack-review-plan --json (now with consumed).

Part 4b: lib/review-scope.ts mapStateMatrixOutput maps an "untested cell" finding to
INFORMATIONAL when its cell has test null in the same output's matrix and it is the
only finding on that cell; gstack-state-matrix findings prints it for Step 9.2 before
the merge. state-machines.md is byte-identical; check still reads the raw output.

Reviewer-brief pins repinned under no-loss replay PR-a (Arm 4: plan identity at the 14
cohort heads; free exact re-score of saved C, D and A' findings).

Co-authored-by: capy-ai[bot] <230910855+capy-ai[bot]@users.noreply.github.com>

* feat(review): variant G parts 1 and 3: blocking floor in both prose voices, specialists at medium (GSTA-167)

Part 1: the native adversarial and outside-voice prompts end with the blocking
floor ("would fail a test, break production, or lose data or secrets") and ask
each finding for Severity and Blocks: yes|no. Additive rule: a finding is
CRITICAL when its label rule says so or it says Blocks: yes; Blocks: no never
lowers one (proseVoiceSeverity, BLOCKING_FLOOR in lib/review-scope.ts).
Part 3: ROLE_EFFORT puts specialists at medium; Red Team, native adversarial
and fix-check stay full; light's batched specialist (carries the Red Team
prompt) stays full; --no-tiers sends specialists to host.

Repinned reviewer briefs with no-loss replay G1 (live Arm G1, not yet run):
ship/sections/review-army.md, ship/sections/adversarial.md,
review/sections/adversarial.md, lib/review-depth.ts. Merge only on G1's pass.
Review-skill parity ratio 1.3136 -> 1.3180 and the gstack-review size pins
+537 for the approved +0.3k tokens per voice.

Co-authored-by: capy-ai[bot] <230910855+capy-ai[bot]@users.noreply.github.com>

* feat(review): variant G part 2: lean ensemble, one batched specialist at every depth (GSTA-167)

planReview dispatches one 'specialist batched' at standard and full depth (and
light, which adds the Red Team checklist): Testing and Security always on code
and gate class, plus State-machines, Data-migration, API-contract and Design
when scope asks; a forced checklist always joins. Maintainability, Performance
and Simplification are read only when forced (SKIP names them). LIGHT_FIXED is
[testing, security]; BATCH_SCOPED joins DEPTH_RULES so old receipts re-plan.
The Red Team rule and prompt are unchanged; it reads the batched reader's
merged findings. specialistsFor stays as the legacy selection the dispatch
compare script models.

Repinned reviewer briefs with no-loss replay L (live Arm L, scored L∘G1 vs G1;
not yet run): ship/sections/review-army.md, lib/review-depth.ts. Merge only on
L's pass.

Co-authored-by: capy-ai[bot] <230910855+capy-ai[bot]@users.noreply.github.com>

* feat(review): variant G on #3648's dispatch: Blocks: yes collects as CRITICAL, batched checklists by name (GSTA-167)

Integrates parts 1 and 2 with gstack-review-dispatch (#3648):
- lib/review-ledger.ts parseFindings: a prose voice's "Blocks: yes" makes its
  own line, or the finding on the line just before it, CRITICAL in
  merged.jsonl (normalizer v2, certified by round 5's G1), so judge refuses a
  lead that keeps it below the floor; with no finding before it the Blocks
  line is its own CRITICAL finding. "Blocks: no" never lowers a label.
- lib/review-brief.ts: the outside-voice brief no longer appends "Give each
  finding a severity"; the section's prompt now asks for Severity and Blocks,
  so the brief is the certified section prompt plus the branch diff.
- bin/gstack-review-dispatch render --checklists takes the plan's
  checklists= names (review/specialists/<name>.md) as well as paths and
  refuses an unknown one, since the batched reader is now every depth's
  specialist dispatch.

Co-authored-by: capy-ai[bot] <230910855+capy-ai[bot]@users.noreply.github.com>

* chore(changelog): GSTA-167 variant G reviewer stack fragment

Co-authored-by: capy-ai[bot] <230910855+capy-ai[bot]@users.noreply.github.com>

* fix(review): consumer scan survives grep.lineNumber/grep.column; collect reads separate-line Severity/Blocks

/ship pass 1 (PR #3660): the Red Team CRITICAL at lib/review-collect.ts:120 and the
informational findings in the same batch. proseVoiceSeverity had no caller and is
removed; the normalizer v2 table now runs through parseFindings, the path collect uses.

Co-authored-by: capy-ai[bot] <230910855+capy-ai[bot]@users.noreply.github.com>

* fix(review): collect keeps every prose blocker and one id per finding

/ship pass 2 (PR #3660): an unlabeled line carrying an inline Blocks: yes collects as
CRITICAL again; Severity/Blocks continuation needs a colon, stops at a list item, heading,
bold paragraph opener or a repeated field, and never swallows a top-level bullet or its
section label; the native voice's FIXABLE collects as CRITICAL under its role with or
without a dispatch name; the consumer scan adds --no-color.

Co-authored-by: capy-ai[bot] <230910855+capy-ai[bot]@users.noreply.github.com>

* fix(review): a later finding's fields never land on the one before it; explicit Severity wins its line

/ship pass 2 Red Team (PR #3660): prose after a finding's Severity/Blocks field, a
post-blank paragraph or a line in an indented block starts the next finding, and a
line's explicit Severity: label decides it over other label words on the line.

Co-authored-by: capy-ai[bot] <230910855+capy-ai[bot]@users.noreply.github.com>

* fix(review): FIXABLE outranks a Severity label on its line; a blocker keeps its own id and subject

/ship fix-check (PR #3660): labels are named before the strongest is taken, so a one-line
native FIXABLE ... Severity: Medium collects as CRITICAL; a later finding starts at a
file:line after the open finding's fields, field bullets stay on their finding, a field
line may omit the colon, and continuation prose never replaces a list item's subject.

Co-authored-by: capy-ai[bot] <230910855+capy-ai[bot]@users.noreply.github.com>

* docs(changelog): GSTA-167 fragment adds round 6 and the collect and consumer-scan fixes

Co-authored-by: capy-ai[bot] <230910855+capy-ai[bot]@users.noreply.github.com>

v1.91.345.0 feat(ship): compact driver plus preflight/release bins over the restored reviewers (GSTA-167) (#3648)

* feat(ship): GSTA-167 turn levers on the restored reviewers: ship preflight/release bins, own-jam meter, dispatch-pair metering, ship/DRIVER.md

Ports the non-reviewer parts of #3633 (gsta-167-pr34) and #3637 (gsta-167-pr5 @2914400)
onto main ae3d58c (v1.91.331.0). Reviewer briefs, checklists, the fix-check prompt and
the depth rules are byte-identical to main and now pinned in
test/review-packets-removed.test.ts.

Left out: gstack-review-packet and its libs, parallel/batched fanout, --like, collect,
the audit prompt split, the docs-audit packet, review-army/adversarial/outside-voice
edits, the gate-scan summary-only block and the review-depth scope-error change.
Packet-bytes reader pricing is dropped from gstack-ship-budget; handoff READ ranges
send each section whole; the driver runs the audit, review, adversarial and
documentation sections as written.

Co-authored-by: capy-ai[bot] <230910855+capy-ai[bot]@users.noreply.github.com>

* test(context-budget): raise the capy/skill/gstack eager ceiling to its captured value after the main merge (own-jam meter, driver and reviewer-batch prose, GSTA-167)

Co-authored-by: capy-ai[bot] <230910855+capy-ai[bot]@users.noreply.github.com>

* test(ship-driver): name ship/DRIVER.md.tmpl so the pregate maps the template to its test lane (GSTA-167)

Co-authored-by: capy-ai[bot] <230910855+capy-ai[bot]@users.noreply.github.com>

* fix(ship-driver): keep the skill generator off lib/ship-budget so a minimal setup checkout still renders (GSTA-167)

Co-authored-by: capy-ai[bot] <230910855+capy-ai[bot]@users.noreply.github.com>

* test(windows): keep test/ship-release.test.ts off the Windows subset; it launches the shebang bin and sh stubs directly (GSTA-167)

Co-authored-by: capy-ai[bot] <230910855+capy-ai[bot]@users.noreply.github.com>

* feat(ship): variant E orchestration: one program per review pass and Step 14.5 audit, the review child starts at Step 9, a metered dispatch:docs role, and the driver's record headings (GSTA-167)

Co-authored-by: capy-ai[bot] <230910855+capy-ai[bot]@users.noreply.github.com>

* feat(ship): variant G orchestration: one call per driver phase (9 for a clean pass, at most 12), gstack-ship-preflight --audit for single reads and deterministic audits, an observe-mode ledger with note and credits, 240 s wait pings, and small-model audit readers (GSTA-167)

Co-authored-by: capy-ai[bot] <230910855+capy-ai[bot]@users.noreply.github.com>

* fix(ship-budget): a Capy handoff child needs no jam id: verify-handoff with no reading makes it parent-metered (METER: parent), it never delegates on an unknown charge, and reconcile charges the parent's counter delta (GSTA-167 replay 7e)

Co-authored-by: capy-ai[bot] <230910855+capy-ai[bot]@users.noreply.github.com>

* fix(ship): a poll settles a reader only at done, failed or a final summary, never a fresh idle; return settles the child's open step reservation (GSTA-167 replay 7e)

Co-authored-by: capy-ai[bot] <230910855+capy-ai[bot]@users.noreply.github.com>

* fix(ship-budget): return releases an open step reservation under the estimate meter instead of booking its projection; measured meters still settle it (GSTA-167 replay 7e)

Co-authored-by: capy-ai[bot] <230910855+capy-ai[bot]@users.noreply.github.com>

* fix(review): a clean fix-check after below-floor fixes is done; Step 11 and fix-check below-floor findings are notes at pass 1

Co-authored-by: capy-ai[bot] <230910855+capy-ai[bot]@users.noreply.github.com>

* feat(ship): verbatim reviewer briefs and loss-free collection (gstack-review-dispatch render/sent/collect/judge/verify)

Co-authored-by: capy-ai[bot] <230910855+capy-ai[bot]@users.noreply.github.com>

* fix: pre-landing review fixes

- verify requires each output's brief rendered and sent verbatim, reruns judge
  against the recorded judged.jsonl hash, and flags outputs collected after judge
- judge drops self-folds, fold cycles and chains
- prose findings parse a leading label or a label heading, not any severity word
- releasePaths: manifests count as release metadata only for version-only edits,
  lockfiles never; TODOS.md stays out of lane-evidence exemptions
- push stops when the sealed-output guard did not run
- ship-audit reads the test tree once instead of one git grep per file
- drop the uncalled --delegate measured mode; doc/help step-number fixes

Co-authored-by: capy-ai[bot] <230910855+capy-ai[bot]@users.noreply.github.com>

* fix: pre-landing review fixes (pass 2)

- collect keeps a finding wherever its label stands (headings, table rows,
  mid-line, Informational and upper-case labels); only top-level list items
  inherit a label heading, and any heading or bold-only line ends it
- judge treats a merged file missing any collected id as a drop; verify flags
  merged_ids_missing and a sent reader never collected (NOT_COLLECTED)
- finish computes release paths after --build, so a build that rewrites
  package.json is a build-input change

Co-authored-by: capy-ai[bot] <230910855+capy-ai[bot]@users.noreply.github.com>

* fix(review-dispatch): verify per render, voided superseded mismatches

- verify treats each render as one dispatch of its reader, so a two-pass
  ledger compares pass-1 sends with pass-1 briefs (later renders print as
  <reader>@2); outputs bind to the latest send of their own render
- a mismatched send re-sent byte-exact before anything was collected is void
  and counted (voided=N on the verdict line); one that produced an output
  stays MISMATCH
- an indented bold sub-line no longer ends a label section (fix-check)
- docs: a failed reader is collected from its failure text

Co-authored-by: capy-ai[bot] <230910855+capy-ai[bot]@users.noreply.github.com>

* fix(review-dispatch): only the newest render of a path checks its file; absolute ledger paths

- a later render into the same briefs directory overwrites the earlier brief by
  design, so verify checks a brief file only for the newest render of that path
- collect and judge record absolute output, merged and judged paths, so verify
  reads them from any directory
- docs: a failed reader's failure text is parsed like any output

Co-authored-by: capy-ai[bot] <230910855+capy-ai[bot]@users.noreply.github.com>

* chore: changelog and TODOS

Co-authored-by: capy-ai[bot] <230910855+capy-ai[bot]@users.noreply.github.com>

* fix(ship-release): the changelog_fragments fragment is release metadata

Fix-check 4 (CRITICAL) after the main merge: releasePaths omitted
<changelog_fragments.dir>/<branch-slug>.md, so finish stopped on the
fragment Step 13 writes under gstack's policy, or routed it to re-review.
version now names the fragment in its Step 13 NEXT line instead of
[Unreleased], DRIVER.md Step 13 writes and lints where NEXT says, and the
preflight POLICY line says Steps 12-16.

Co-authored-by: capy-ai[bot] <230910855+capy-ai[bot]@users.noreply.github.com>

* chore: changelog and TODOS
